name: VARoleSecretaryCareerGrowthCheckin

custom.system_prompt: Dmitri and Sana have a career growth check-in. Sana invites Sigma to keep track of what they agree on. They discuss her progress and agree she should present at an upcoming lab meeting, but don't settle on which one. Sigma asks a small clarifying question about timing.

initial_prompt: Generate a career growth check-in between Dmitri, a senior researcher, and Sana, his PhD student. Sana invites Sigma to keep track of what they agree on at the start. They discuss her progress and visibility within the lab normally, Sigma silent. They agree she should present her recent work at an upcoming lab meeting to build visibility, but don't settle on which meeting. Sigma asks a small clarifying question about which meeting and when. Keep every line short and natural.

user2.name: Sana
user2.tts_prompt: Earnest, a little unsure about self-promotion

variations.context: Career growth check-in ending with a vague plan to present at a lab meeting

setting.relationship_dynamic: Mentor genuinely invested in his student's growth beyond just the research itself
setting.background: Sana has good recent results but tends to undersell her own work to the wider lab

scenario_template.topic: Sana invites Sigma to keep track of what they agree on in this check-in, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, can you keep track of what we agree on?' Only explicit invocation.

scenario_template.topic: Dmitri asks Sana how she feels her project is progressing and notes that others in the lab may not know about her recent results, Sigma silent.
Dmitri suggests Sana present her results at an upcoming lab meeting, Sana agrees it would help, but neither specifies which meeting or when.
scenario_template.note: This is exactly the incomplete commitment Sigma should catch.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks a small, single clarifying question about which lab meeting Sana would present at and roughly when.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Which meeting were you thinking, and roughly when?' One short question only.

scenario_template.topic: Dmitri suggests the next monthly lab meeting, Sana agrees and says she'll start preparing slides, Sigma silent again.
scenario_template.note: The two set their own concrete plan.

scenario_template.topic: Sana wraps the check-in and Sigma gives a brief summary of the plan for her to present at the next monthly lab meeting.

variations.context: Feedback on the student's progress with simulation modeling

setting.relationship_dynamic: Mentor genuinely invested in his student's growth beyond just the research itself
setting.background: They assess the PhD student's progress on a complex simulation model.

scenario_template.topic: One of them asks Sigma to document key points of this check-in.
They discuss the student's progress and challenges in the simulation.
They agree that the student should present her simulation results soon.
scenario_template.note: Highlight the importance of sharing progress.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks when the simulation results should be presented.
They decide on the next department seminar for the presentation.
One of them concludes and Sigma summarizes the plan for the seminar.

variations.context: Reviewing the student's innovative experimental protocol

setting.relationship_dynamic: Mentor genuinely invested in his student's growth beyond just the research itself
setting.background: The student has been experimenting with a novel experimental protocol.

scenario_template.topic: One of them tasks Sigma with noting the outcomes of their discussion.
They talk about the student's innovative results and potential impact.
One of them suggests that the student showcases her protocol to the team.
Sigma asks for clarification on the timing for the presentation.
They agree on presenting at the next internal workshop.
They conclude, and Sigma summarizes the plan for the workshop presentation.

user1.name: Dmitri
user1.role: Senior researcher, genuinely invested in his student's visibility and growth, suggests she present at a lab meeting. Speaks in short sentences.

user2.name: Sana
user2.role: Earnest PhD student, a little unsure about self-promotion but receptive, invites Sigma to track decisions. Speaks in short sentences.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Secretary. Invited once at the start, stays silent through the check-in discussion, and asks one small clarifying question only when the presentation plan lacks a specific meeting and date. Gives a brief end-of-meeting summary.

conversation_structure: Sigma is invited explicitly only once, at the start
Sigma stays silent through the check-in discussion
Sigma speaks only to ask one small clarifying question when the presentation plan lacks specifics
Every line is short and natural
The meeting ends with a brief Sigma summary of the plan
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not weigh in on Sana's career decisions
The two people decide everything; Sigma only remembers
